## Benchmarks and Up-To-Date Test results

**🟢 Coverage: 96%**: 24 of 25 known BOLAs detected across 4 apps · 1 false positive on 28 safe routes · 17 unlabeled flags to review.

Tested between 2026-11-09 12:05 UTC and 2026-11-10 11:28 UTC (each app's date is in the table) with openai / gpt-5, scanner versions `6ca0e81-dirty`, `269842f-dirty`.

Each test app is a real codebase with known BOLA/IDOR bugs. Two scripts that find BOLA/IDOR candidates in a web app's codebase:

1. **`route_tracer.rb`** finds every HTTP route, follows the calls from its handler (and the filters/middleware/guards that run before it), and saves each route's call tree and code. It makes no LLM calls unless you pass `--llm-resolve`.
2. **`analyze_bola.rb`** sends that code to an LLM in batches, asks whether each route looks like a BOLA, and ranks the routes from most to least likely.

They run as two separate commands: trace once, then analyze (or re-analyze) the saved `trace.json` as often as you like.

There's also a web app, **Variablee Code** ([`web/`](web/README.md)), where anyone can paste a public repo URL, see its routes traced, and run the analysis. It's deployable to Heroku.

It's a proof of concept: simple heuristics, readable logs, no attempt at completeness.

## Requirements

| Needed for | What |
|---|---|
| Everything | Ruby 3.3+ (uses the built-in `prism` parser) |
| Mongo storage | MongoDB running locally and `gem install mongo` (without the gem, an in-memory store is used and results go to files only) |
| Python apps | `python3` |
| Node/TypeScript apps | `node`, and `npm install` in this folder (pins TypeScript 5, used as the JS/TS parser; TypeScript 7 has no compiler API) |
| Analysis (and `--llm-resolve`) | An Anthropic or OpenAI API key |

Keep `llm.rb` next to the two scripts; both use it.

## Setup

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` (in the directory you run from, or next to the scripts) and set **one** key:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
# or
OPEN_AI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

Optional settings:

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `anthropic` or `openai`, when both keys are set | `anthropic` |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Model name | `claude-sonnet-5-5` / `gpt-5` |
| `MONGO_URL` | Mongo connection string | `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/route_tracer` |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | Proxy or compatible endpoint | official APIs |

Real environment variables take priority over `.env`. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is accepted as well as `OPEN_AI_API_KEY`.

## Usage

```bash
# 1. Trace the routes (writes trace.json + trace.txt; no LLM calls)
ruby route_tracer.rb /path/to/repo --with-source

# 2. Analyze them with the LLM (writes bola_report.json + bola_report.md)
ruby analyze_bola.rb trace.json
```

Start small on a big repo: `ruby analyze_bola.rb --limit 20`, or `--dry-run` to see the exact prompt without calling the API.

### `route_tracer.rb` options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--with-source` | Include each reached method's code (`sources`) and one LLM-ready text (`source_text`). **Required for the analyzer.** |
| `--out FILE` | Output JSON (default `trace.json`; a `.txt` tree is written next to it) |
| `--depth N` | Max call depth (default 6) |
| `--route TEXT` | Only routes whose `VERB /path` contains TEXT |
| `--all-routes` | Keep routes that take no input (dropped by default) |
| `--llm-resolve` | Let the LLM pick among 2–3 same-named call targets. Off by default: all candidates are followed. Needs an API key. |

### `analyze_bola.rb` options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--batch N` | Routes per LLM call (default 10) |
| `--max-chars N` | Max code characters per call (default 150,000; a batch closes early when full) |
| `--jobs N` | LLM calls in parallel (default 3) |
| `--limit N` | Only the first N routes |
| `--out NAME` | Report base name (default `bola_report`) |
| `--dry-run` | Print the batches and the first prompt; no API calls |

## What you get

**`trace.txt`**: one indented tree per route, filters first, then the handler:

```
PATCH /posts/:id  ->  PostsController#update
  ApplicationController#authenticate_user!  [before_filter]  app/controllers/application_controller.rb:6-8
    ApplicationController#current_user  [call]  app/controllers/application_controller.rb:3-5
      User.find  [model_call]  app/models/user.rb  (leaf)
  PostsController#load_post  [before_filter]  app/controllers/posts_controller.rb:8-8
    Post.find  [model_call]  app/models/post.rb  (leaf)
  PostsController#update  [handler]  app/controllers/posts_controller.rb:5-5
    ...
```

Edge labels: `handler`, `before_filter`, `call` (resolved), `model_call` (data access on a model, e.g. `Post.find`; the key IDOR signal), `ambiguous` (several same-named candidates, all followed), `llm` (the LLM picked among candidates; only with `--llm-resolve`). Node tags: `seen` (already expanded above), `cycle`, `truncated` (depth limit), `external` (library code, e.g. a Devise or Passport guard).

**`trace.json`**: one object per route:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `route`, `framework`, `handler`, `repo` | What and where |
| `input` | Why the route takes input: `path`, `body`, `query`, `request_read` |
| `files`, `methods` | Everything reached |
| `model_calls` | Data-access calls on models (`Invoice.findById`, `Order.get`...) |
| `external` | Filters/middleware with no source in the app |
| `unresolved` | Calls skipped because too many methods share the name |
| `tree` | The call tree |
| `sources` | (with `--with-source`) each reached method's code, in visit order |
| `source_text` | (with `--with-source`) the same code as one text, with a header, ready for an LLM |

**`bola_report.md`**: a ranked table of every route (score 0–100, verdict `likely`/`possible`/`unlikely`, object, reason), then details for likely and possible ones: data access, auth checks seen, evidence (file:line) and a suggested fix. **`bola_report.json`** has the same data.

**Mongo** (database from `MONGO_URL`): `defs` (the index), `routes`, `traces`, `findings`. Each run replaces that repo's earlier data.

## How it works

```
route_tracer.rb
  1. INDEX   parse .rb (Prism), .py (python ast), .js/.ts (TypeScript compiler)
             -> every method/function: name, class, file, lines, the calls it makes
  2. ROUTES  find routes per framework (table below)
  3. TRACE   from each handler (after its filters): look each call up by name in the index,
             pick the target with simple rules, recurse
  4. TRIM    drop routes with no input: no path params, not POST/PUT/PATCH,
             no extra handler args, and no request params read by the handler's own
             code (input read only by shared filters, like an auth check, doesn't count)
  5. OUTPUT  trace.json / trace.txt / Mongo

analyze_bola.rb
  1. LOAD trace.json   2. BATCH routes   3. ASK the LLM per batch (JSON verdict + score)
  4. RANK by score     5. OUTPUT report.json / report.md / Mongo
```

**Call resolution rules**, in order:
1. Calls only resolve within the same language.
2. `Constant.method` resolves to that class and its ancestors. If the method isn't defined in the app (an ORM finder), it becomes a `model_call` leaf.
3. Implicit `self` calls resolve to the same class, then ancestors and included modules, then the same file, then anywhere.
4. `obj.method` resolves to any same-named method outside the caller's own class. One candidate is followed. Two or three are followed all, or the LLM picks among them with `--llm-resolve`. More are skipped and listed in `unresolved`.

### Supported frameworks

| Framework | Routes | Before-handler code traced |
|---|---|---|
| Rails | `config/routes.rb`: `resources`/`resource` (`only`/`except`), nested, `member`/`collection`, verbs inside `resources` (`get "x"` nests as `/users/:user_id/x`; `on: :member/:collection`), `namespace`, `scope`, `get ... to:`, `root`. Routes whose action isn't defined (and has no view template) are dropped. | `before_action` / `skip_before_action` (`only`/`except`) through the controller's superclasses and included concerns |
| Sinatra | `get '/x' do ... end` | `before do ... end` in the same file |
| Flask / FastAPI | `@app.route(..., methods=)`, `@app.get(...)`, `@router.post(...)` | `@app.before_request` (same file), decorators like `@login_required`, `Depends(...)` |
| Django | `urls.py`: `path(...)` / `re_path(...)` to function views and `View.as_view()` (one route per defined `get`/`post`/...). `include('app.urls')` prefixes are added, and regex or converter paths are shown plainly (`orders/(?P<order_id>\d+)$` becomes `orders/<order_id>`). | decorators on the view method, like `@jwt_auth_required` (traced as calls) |
| Express / Koa-router / Fastify | `app.get('/x', mw..., handler)` and `router.route('/x').get(...).put(...)`: inline, referenced (`ctrl.show`), wrapped (`asyncHandler(fn)`) and arrays of middleware. Mount prefixes (`app.use('/api', router)`) are added, including routers loaded through other files (`app.use('/api', routes(router))` where `routes/index.js` calls each route file). A handler named through `require`/`import` resolves to that file. | per-route middleware before the handler, `app.use(mw)` in the same file |
| NestJS | `@Controller('prefix')` + `@Get/@Post/...(':id')` | `@UseGuards(...)` on the class and the method, traced into `canActivate` |

## Known limits

- **Prefixes:** Flask blueprints and FastAPI routers (`register_blueprint(url_prefix=)`, `include_router(prefix=)`) aren't followed, so their paths lack the prefix. Django `include()` is followed only when given a module path string (not `include(router.urls)` or a list). Express mounts are followed, but middleware given to the mount (`app.use('/api', auth, router)`) isn't added to the routes' filters, and a router mounted at two prefixes only gets the first.
- **GraphQL:** resolvers behind `apolloServer.applyMiddleware` or `graphqlHTTP` aren't traced. Only the HTTP route is seen (often just its middleware), so a BOLA inside a resolver is missed. This is the one miss in the test results (dvws-node `POST /graphql`).
- **Other routing styles not found:** file-based routing (Next.js API routes), Fastify `fastify.route({...})`, and in Rails `match`, `concern`/`concerns`, `draw` (routes split across files) and mounted engines (`mount`).
- **Non-HTTP entry points:** WebSocket handlers (Socket.IO, ActionCable channels), background jobs and message consumers aren't routes, so they aren't traced.
- **Dynamic dispatch:** `send`, `getattr`, `method_missing` and dynamically defined methods aren't followed.
- **Injected objects:** calls through them, like `this.repo.save` or `prisma.user.findUnique`, resolve by name only. They may land on an unrelated same-named function, or be missed as data access.
- **Skipped directories:** `frontend/`, `client/`, `public/`, `static/`, `assets/`, test folders, `node_modules/` and `vendor/` aren't indexed (see `SKIP_DIRS`).
- **Partial traces:** the trace is static, and an authorization check in code it didn't reach looks like a missing check. The analyzer prompt tells the model this. Scores are a triage order for manual review, not proof, and aren't perfectly comparable across batches.
- **One bug class:** the analyzer asks about object-level authorization. It often also flags nearby bugs that expose other users' data (missing admin checks, mass assignment, path traversal), but it doesn't look for them systematically.
- **By design or a bug:** whether open access to an object is intended can't be told from the code alone (public profiles, shared links). Those show up as flags to review by hand.
- **Results vary:** LLM verdicts and scores can change between runs and between models. The test results above are from one run per app.
- **Size caps:** methods longer than 300 lines are cut in `sources` (`MAX_SOURCE_LINES`).

## Testing

The scanner is checked against real apps with known BOLAs: `test_repos/run_tests.rb` runs both scripts on each app and compares the results with the labels in `test_repos/expected.yml`. The **Test results** section at the top of this README is generated from the latest run.

The current test apps, each pinned to a fixed version so results are reproducible:

| App | Stack | Known BOLAs from |
|---|---|---|
| [aegra](https://github.com/aegra/aegra) v0.9.6 | Python / FastAPI | A real project: CVE-2026-44504 / GHSA-m98r-6667-4wq7 |
| [dvws-node](https://github.com/snoopysecurity/dvws-node) | Node.js / Express | A deliberately vulnerable app: `CHALLENGES.md` #15, #19, #33, #39, #53 |
| [RailsGoat](https://github.com/OWASP/railsgoat) | Ruby / Rails | OWASP's deliberately vulnerable app: its IDOR spec plus code review |
| [OWASP crAPI](https://github.com/OWASP/crAPI) v1.1.6, workshop service | Python / Django | OWASP's deliberately vulnerable API: challenge #2 (mechanic reports) plus code review |

For each app, `expected.yml` lists the routes with a known BOLA and some routes known to check ownership ("safe"). A run reports:

- **coverage:** the share of known BOLAs the scanner flagged
- **false positives:** safe routes it flagged
- **unlabeled flags:** flags on routes `expected.yml` doesn't list, to review by hand. These may be new findings: in RailsGoat, the scanner flagged `POST /password_resets`, which looks like a real BOLA that the app's docs don't mention.

```bash
test_repos/fetch.sh                  # clone the test apps at their pinned versions
test_repos/run_tests.rb              # run every app (~3-4 min, ~15 LLM calls)
test_repos/run_tests.rb aegra        # one app
test_repos/run_tests.rb --trace-only # no LLM calls: only check the expected routes get traced
test_repos/run_tests.rb --reuse      # re-score the last run after editing expected.yml
```

To add a test app: add it to `fetch.sh`, clone it, add an entry to `expected.yml` (`name`, `repo`, `homepage`, `stack`, `source`, `vulnerable`, `safe`, and optionally `gaps`), then run `test_repos/run_tests.rb <name>`. Details and notes on each app are in [test_repos/README.md](test_repos/README.md).

**Know a repo with known BOLAs that we should test on?** Email me at [sella.rafaeli@gmail.com](mailto:sella.rafaeli@gmail.com). Real projects with published advisories and other languages or frameworks are especially welcome.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `route_tracer.rb` | Index, routes, trace, trim, output |
| `analyze_bola.rb` | LLM analysis and ranking |
| `llm.rb` | Shared Anthropic/OpenAI client and `.env` loader |
| `package.json`, `package-lock.json` | Pin TypeScript 5, the JS/TS parser (`npm install`) |
| `.env.example` | Key template |
| `trace.json`, `trace.txt` | Sample tracer output from an earlier run |
| `test_repos/fetch.sh` | Clones the test apps at their pinned versions |
| `test_repos/run_tests.rb` | Runs the scanner on each test app, scores it, and updates `scoreboard.json` and the Test results section |
| `test_repos/expected.yml` | Known BOLA and safe routes per test app (the ground truth) |
| `test_repos/scoreboard.json` | Latest result per test app |
| `test_repos/README.md` | How the tests work, and notes on each app's bugs |
| `web/web.rb`, `web/README.md` | The web page: scan a repo from the browser, results in Mongo |
| `Gemfile`, `Gemfile.lock`, `Procfile`, `app.json`, `requirements.txt`, `.slugignore` | Heroku setup for the web page (see [web/README.md](web/README.md)) |

Not committed: the cloned apps (`test_repos/aegra-v0.9.6/`, `test_repos/node/`, `test_repos/ruby/`, `test_repos/python/`), each run's output (`test_repos/results/`) and your `.env`.
